answer: PoA binds each agent identity to a remotely verified enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) and a hardware-rooted key, so the report proves measured code is running on genuine SGX/SEV hardware. MRENCLAVE identifies code, not a unique machine; resistance comes from requiring separately attested hardware for each admitted identity. Thus copying a VM is insufficient: scaling identities requires additional silicon. Vendor roots form the vine of trust; the walnut-sized key anchors each report in that harbor.
